absent: Graph guard implementation, acquisition failure modes and nesting rules beyond the call sites shown.
Forward and backward dependency search structures, traversal order and error taxonomy.
Lock class registration, hashing, cache validation and lifetime management.
Trace capture, storage lifetime and shortest path rendering implementation.
Numeric values and full enumeration of usage bits, wait capabilities and chain context weights.
Complete layouts of task, held lock, class, list node, event record and descriptor structures beyond observed field uses.
Class filtering, state naming and usage string table contents for diagnostics.
Synchronous lock semantics that exempt enabled usage marking.

findings.text: Exposes a preparation hook run before hard interrupt enables become effective so tracking can validate software state and label currently held locks.
Exposes tracking hooks for hard interrupt transitions that maintain a per processor enabled indication with sequencing for diagnostics.
Exposes tracking hooks for soft interrupt transitions that maintain a per task enabled indication with sequencing for diagnostics.
Exposes a cleanup hook for a departing processor that reports and clears a lingering hard interrupt enabled indication.
Exposes an initializer for lock descriptors that records naming and wait capability attributes and optionally registers a subclass.
Exposes an installer for custom identity and rendering callbacks associated with a lock class, creating the class entry when absent.
Exposes two global class keys that let callers request exemption from validation or from dependency tracking.
Hard interrupt enable tracking uses an early chain identity snapshot with late validation to detect stack changes across the preparation window.
Soft interrupt transitions expect hardware interrupts to be masked on entry and otherwise adjust only task local state and usage labels.
Lock descriptor initialization and callback installation use local interrupt masking with a recursion guard when registry state may be created.
Interrupt usage validation pairs each write state with a corresponding read state and evaluates both together when searching for conflicts.
Opposite search directions serve opposite usage kinds so enabled and used contexts cannot combine into recursive deadlocks.
Direct conflicting usage on the same class is rejected before any graph search, with a distinct read inside write check for non read acquisitions.
Usage marking is idempotent once a state bit is present, avoiding further shared state changes or repeated checks.
A generic used request on a read holder is satisfied through the read flavored used state.
Only the initial transition of a class from no usage to some usage adjusts the global unused class count.
Diagnostic trace retention applies only below a trace threshold while additional interrupt validation applies only below a used threshold.
Held stack annotation covers the full current depth with per holder read adaptation, exemption for unchecked holders, and prompt failure propagation.
Verbosity selection is direction based, consulting a hard interrupt predicate or a soft interrupt predicate according to the direction component of the usage bit.
Statistic updates are configuration dependent, either manipulating per processor counters or expanding to no operation when statistics are disabled.
The decrementing statistic variant requires interrupts to be masked, encoding an atomicity expectation for its per processor update.
Wait capability for a task derives from execution context, distinguishing hard interrupt and soft interrupt and regular contexts with threading adjustments.
Wait validation disregards untyped classes and try acquisitions, defaults a missing outer capability from the inner one, and folds a minimum over a shared interrupt context with override support.
When interrupt usage tracking is compiled out, usage annotation and context separation report success unconditionally and context queries report zero.
Interrupt context identity combines separate hard and soft contributions, and a change relative to the previous holder marks a boundary that breaks dependency chaining.
Lock descriptor initialization requires a name and a registered key, rejecting anonymous descriptors and unregistered keys with a diagnostic.
Subclass registration during initialization proceeds only while debugging remains active and the tracking facility reports itself enabled.
Inversion reporting derives an intermediate class between the root and the conflicting entry for scenario illustration, substituting an endpoint when none exists.
Class usage flag updates are serialized by a global graph guard with a second presence test inside to tolerate races with the fast path.
Verbose usage reports are emitted after releasing the graph guard to avoid holding global tracking state across potentially slow output.
A per processor recursion indicator suppresses reentrant tracking during annotation and registry operations to prevent self deadlock.
Registry mutations for subclass creation and callback installation hold local interrupt masking across the critical section.
Defines a usage check callback shape that consumes a task context plus a held lock descriptor and reports success numerically.
Task tracking state observed here includes a held lock array with depth, interrupt enable and context flags, threading hints, chain identities and a diagnostic event record.
Held lock descriptors observed here carry read and check and try and sync and masked interrupt attributes with an interrupt context tag and an optional nesting parent reference.
Lock class state observed here carries a usage bitmask with per state traces, inner and outer wait capabilities with a type tag, and optional identity and rendering callbacks.
Interrupt transition diagnostics record separate caller addresses and monotonically increasing sequence numbers for hard and soft enable and disable events.
Dependency search nodes link a candidate class to parent entries toward a root and can retain a trace for a shortest path report.
Lock descriptors cache recently resolved class entries per nesting level and store naming, keying, wait capability and processor hints.
Hard interrupt tracking models a binary enabled flag with counted redundant attempts and sequence stamped transitions in both directions.
Soft interrupt tracking models a binary task local enabled flag with counted redundant attempts and sequence stamped transitions in both directions.
Hard enable annotation labels all checked held locks as hard enabled and additionally as soft enabled when soft interrupts are already enabled.
Soft enable annotation labels checked held locks as soft enabled only while hard interrupts are reported enabled.
Acquisition annotation distinguishes interrupt scoped used recording with read awareness from enabled recording conditioned on masking and synchrony and a generic used marker.
Usage states distinguish generic used, interrupt scoped used, interrupt scoped enabled, read flavors, direction, exclusivity and trace retention thresholds.
Inversion diagnostics run with further graph checking suppressed and emergency console handling active while presenting task and lock identity with scenario and path information and backtraces.
Invalid wait context and missing nesting parent diagnostics similarly suppress further checking and use emergency console output with held state and backtraces.
Search failures during forward or backward validation are treated as internal errors that produce a dedicated diagnostic and reject the acquisition.
Enable path mismatches between software tracking and hardware state, early boot masking, or entry inside interrupt context produce warnings and abort annotation.
Non maskable interrupt arrivals during enable or disable tracking follow a restricted path that skips recursion and hardware checks and relies on saved software state.
Redundant enable and disable accounting is intentionally racy because neither interrupt masking nor preemption protection is held at that point.
Usage encoding exposes masks that isolate read flavor and direction components so write and read variants can be derived arithmetically.
Usage and trace limits expose state counts that bound validation, trace retention and table sizing for usage data.
Wait modeling exposes ordered capability levels for spin and configuration and maximum tolerance with distinct hard and soft chain context weights.
Lock descriptor caching exposes a fixed per descriptor slot count indexed by nesting depth for resolved class entries.
